priority: MUSE_BUILD_ORDER Priority 1 (Independent Learning), items 2, 3, and 4; handoff section 8 weak uncertainty calibration / excessive abstention. This experiment builds directly on the graded reference-purity result (Partially demonstrated, 2026-11-03): its PRIMARY criterion 5 and criteria 1, 2, 3, 4, and 7 PASSed on both cohorts, and its SOLE failure was criterion 6 on the additional cohort - caused entirely by ONE stationary control state (checkpoint 32, seed 383017) at which the candidate abstained on all 16 tasks, downstream of the ABSTENTION branch (opposed_count == 2 with its carried-over authority armed on stationary evidence, realized reference purity 0.886). The same branch was also the candidate's sole remaining non-recent8 checkpoint-32 state on the additional cohort (a return-A abstention, seed 383041, 0 successes / 0 harm vs recent8's 2/14 there, while a recovery the purity gate had disarmed scored 13/3 for the ungated minority method at that state). The structural cause is recorded in the graded report and in the campaign's selected limitation: after the purity gate, the abstention branch is the family's ONLY branch with no expiry or release condition of any kind - its arming is still armed iff NOT stable_disagreement, unchanged since the graded evidence-opposition guard - while the regular recovery branch carries the three-leg authority condition plus the purity gate and the minority branch carries its fraction arming plus the purity gate. Late or stationary abstention firing has now cost graded criteria in three experiments: the joint-concordance experiment (an additional B1 checkpoint-32 abstention costing 9 successes inside its criterion-5 failure), the long-disagreement experiment (a development return-A checkpoint-32 abstention that was the single non-recent8 late state and failed criterion 5 by exactly 1 success), and the reference-purity experiment (the two additional-cohort states above). This cycle changes exactly one thing: it subjects the ABSTENTION branch - and only that branch - to a RELEASE GATE with two legs, both computed from quantities this candidate family already computes on the observed stream alone: (P) the reference-purity arming already frozen for the recovery branches (reference_purity >= 0.70, quantity and threshold unchanged), which is segment-pure at onset and mixed by checkpoint 32 of every switch stage; and (S) ACTING-WINDOW OPPOSITION SUPPORT - the opposed count over the last 8 observed events (each scored against the same extended-reference per-span majorities) must reach at least 3, i.e. the triggering newest pair must be corroborated by at least one further opposed event among the 6 acting-window events preceding it. This cycle's headline criterion is therefore criterion 6, stationary-control selectivity, graded as PRIMARY (it is the preceding experiment's sole failure); criterion 5 (release by checkpoint 32, now with an explicit zero-abstention sub-condition) and criteria 1 and 4 (the onset harm profiles abstention helps protect) are the co-graded guards the gate must not give back.
capability_under_test: Abstention-branch late / stationary firing without release: whether an evidence-derived release condition on the abstention branch can restore stationary selectivity (control successes at least recent8 - 6, control harm at or below recent8, control abstentions at most 32 of 240, per cohort) and remove late abstention from the switch-stage checkpoint-32 records (abstained branch taken in 0 of 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states, from decision records alone), without giving back the onset harm protection abstention provides (criteria 1, 3, and 4 at the graded reference-purity levels) or the now-graded checkpoint-32 release of the recovery branches (criterion 5's carried sub-conditions) - against recent8, cumulative, frozen_A, the evidence-opposition guard, and the minority-archive and reference-purity candidates as baselines, the reference-purity candidate being the decisive comparison (identical but for the abstention release gate). Priority 1 items 2 + 3 + 4 (strengthen long-term retention; prevent new learning from overwriting established knowledge; improve adaptation to changing environments); handoff section 8 weak uncertainty calibration and excessive abstention.
hypothesis: The graded records localize the remaining failure to the abstention branch's ABSENCE of any release condition, not to its trigger: its trigger (opposed_count == 2 against the extended reference) and its carried-over arming (armed iff NOT stable_disagreement) are exactly the graded guard's, and on stationary evidence that arming is satisfied by construction (a stationary local window does not stably disagree with the archive), so the branch stays armed at every checkpoint of every arm forever, and any chance opposed pair - per-event opposed probability about 0.1625 raw (the composed disagreement rate), about 0.13 after the matched-share adjustment - fires a full 16-task abstention. Two already-computed observed-stream summaries separate the populations the branch must keep (onset states, where abstention is the family's only protective response at B1 onset and a real contributor at B2) from the populations it must leave (stationary states and checkpoint-32 states), and this cycle gates the branch on both. LEG P (reference purity, unchanged quantity and threshold 0.70): at every onset checkpoint the reference window is segment-pure or 48/2 (design purity 0.8375 at checkpoint 2, 0.8105 at checkpoint 4), so the leg is armed with design probability about 0.95 or better per onset state - realized in the graded purity experiment at EVERY pooled onset state on both cohorts (B2 onset realized purity 0.784-0.900 development, 0.795-0.889 additional; zero onset states purity-disarmed on either cohort) - while at checkpoint 32 of every switch stage the reference is a 30/20 mix (global design purity 0.5675; realized 0.645-0.758 development and 0.658-0.810 additional in the graded purity experiment, self-fit inflated above design, with the purity gate armed at only 3 of 9 checkpoint-32 states on each cohort), so leg P alone releases roughly two-thirds of late abstention exposure. LEG S (acting-window opposition support, threshold: opposed count over the last 8 events >= 3): the triggering pair must not be the only opposition in the acting window. An event following the same rule as the reference majority is opposed with probability about 0.1625 raw / 0.13 matched-adjusted; an event following the opposite rule with probability about 0.8375 raw / 0.67 adjusted. At a stationary state (and at checkpoint-2 onset, where the 6 preceding acting-window events are previous-segment), the probability of at least one supporting opposed event among those 6 is therefore about 0.57-0.66; at checkpoint-4 onset (2 current-rule + 4 previous-rule among the 6) it is about 0.94-0.99. Leg S thus retains roughly 57-66 percent of checkpoint-2 abstention firings and 94-99 percent of checkpoint-4 firings (pooled onset retention about 0.75 before leg P, about 0.72-0.75 combined), while a stationary trigger survives it only about 57-66 percent of the time - applied to an already rare event (graded control abstention states across the last three experiments in this line: 0/15, 0/15, 0/15, and 1/15 per cohort-experiment, the 1 being the graded purity failure). Combined, the two legs are designed to retain about three-quarters of the reference-purity candidate's onset abstentions (32/288 pooled onset abstentions on both graded purity cohorts, worth harm margins of 58 and 85 against the guard under criterion 3, so a one-quarter thinning is designed to cost roughly 5-11 pooled onset harm against those margins), to cut stationary abstention firing to roughly 0.1-0.2 expected states per cohort, and to cut checkpoint-32 abstention survival to roughly 0.33 (leg P armed share) x 0.6 (leg S) = about 0.20 per triggered late state. Two honest limits are pre-registered, not hidden: (1) a flipped pair on stationary evidence is LOCALLY IDENTICAL to a genuine onset pair - the newest events, the acting window, the local window, the reference, and the archive have the same distributions in the two cases - so NO observed-stream condition can separate them individually; this gate does not claim to identify the cause of a pair, it raises the evidence bar (corroboration) and bounds the branch by reference composition (purity), trading a quantified share of onset protection for release, and both sides of that trade are graded (criteria 1/3/4 against criteria 6/5). In particular leg P does NOT disarm the exact graded stationary failure state (its realized purity was 0.886, armed): if a stationary pair with a supporting opposed event fires on these NEW cohorts, criterion 6 fails again and that is charged, not excused. (2) Leg P's late release is weaker on realized values than on global design values because of the same self-fit compression the purity protocol pre-registered (realized checkpoint-32 purity armed at 3 of 9 states, not the roughly 0.3 of 9 the global design value suggests); the criterion-5 abstention sub-condition (0 of 9) is graded against the realized behavior, not the design arithmetic.
limitation_evidence: REFERENCE_PURITY_GATED_RECOVERY (docs/REFERENCE_PURITY_GATED_RECOVERY.md, graded Partially demonstrated, 2026-11-03, cohorts 382003-family / 383001-family now INSPECTED): PRIMARY criterion 5 PASS on both cohorts, criteria 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 PASS on both, criterion 6 FAIL on the additional cohort only; NOT Failed and NOT a Regression under the protocol's own definitions.

Same experiment, criterion-6 decomposition (the selected limitation, first prong): additional control abstentions 16/240 PASS and harm 114 vs recent8 120 PASS, but successes 110 vs recent8 120 (required at least 114) FAIL - the entire deficit is ONE state: control checkpoint 32, seed 383017, abstained on all 16 tasks (0 successes / 0 harm vs recent8's 10/6 there), downstream of the abstention branch: opposed_count == 2 with its carried-over authority armed on stationary evidence, at realized reference purity 0.886. The candidate was identical to the minority baseline method AND to the guard method on every pooled control figure on that cohort, and the purity gate changed nothing on the stationary arm on either cohort, by design (abstention was deliberately not purity-gated in that protocol; its expected failure mode 4 charged late abstention under criterion 5 only). Development control passed with abstentions 0/240, successes 124 vs recent8 118, harm 116 vs 122 - including one productive control recovery at checkpoint 2 (seed 382039) that offset nothing on the additional cohort.

Same experiment, criterion-5 decomposition (the selected limitation, second prong): additional checkpoint-32 abstentions 16/144, successes 64 vs recent8 66, non-recent8 branch in 1 of 9 states - PASS - but that one remaining state is a return-A ABSTENTION (seed 383041, 0 successes / 0 harm vs recent8's 2/14 there): the purity gate disarmed four late recovery triggers on that cohort (records-only minority-rule derivation 4/9 non-recent8 states, recovery_disarmed_by_purity true at all four, realized purity 0.684-0.697), and the only branch still able to take a late state was the one branch with no gate of any kind. At that same state the ungated minority method scored 13 successes / 3 harm through a recovery - the abstention was not even the best available late response there. Development's one non-recent8 checkpoint-32 state was a B2 minority routing at purity 0.727 (7/9 vs recent8 8/8).

Same experiment, the profile that must not be given back: pooled onset harm 137 vs guard 195 (development) and 133 vs guard 218 (additional), 6/6 cells at or below recent8 on both cohorts (criterion 3 PASS both); B2 pooled onset harm 48 vs guard 64 and 49 vs guard 78, minority recovery TAKEN 5/6 and 4/6 at B2 onset (criterion 1 PASS both); return-A pooled harm 37 vs guard 79 and 29 vs guard 54 (criterion 4 PASS both); return-A successes 59 / 67 (criterion 2 PASS both); pooled onset abstentions 32/288 on BOTH cohorts - the abstention branch's onset contribution this gate thins by design (hypothesis arithmetic: retention about 0.72-0.75 pooled, designed cost roughly 5-11 pooled onset harm against criterion-3 margins of 58 / 85). Checkpoint-32 abstentions were 0/144 development and 16/144 additional - the additional figure is entirely the return-A abstention state above.

Earlier instances of the same branch costing graded criteria (the limitation is recurrent, not a single draw): JOINT_CONCORDANCE_RECOVERY (graded Failed, 2026-10-30) - one additional B1 checkpoint-32 abstention cost 9 successes inside its criterion-5 failure on that cohort. LONG_DISAGREEMENT_JOINT_RECOVERY (graded Failed, 2026-11-01) - development criterion 5 FAILed by exactly 1 success (33 vs recent8 42, required 34), the single non-recent8 checkpoint-32 state being one late abstention at return-A checkpoint 32, seed 352003. MINORITY_ARCHIVE_JOINT_RECOVERY (graded Failed / Regression, 2026-11-02) - abstention released perfectly there (0/144 at checkpoint 32 on both cohorts), which is why the purity protocol left it ungated; the reference-purity cohorts show that release was cohort luck, not a property of the branch: its arming condition has no term that can turn it off on stationary or late evidence.

Structural diagnosis from the graded records: every other branch of the family now carries an evidence-derived release condition - regular recovery: three-leg authority (local disagreement / corroboration / long disagreement) PLUS the reference-purity gate; minority recovery: fraction arming (a static bound, shown insufficient alone by the minority experiment) PLUS the purity gate. Abstention's arming (armed iff NOT stable_disagreement) was designed in the bounded-authority experiment to DISARM the branch at a return onset (where the local window is the reversed segment) - a switch-onset condition, not a release condition: on stationary evidence and late in any stage whose current rule agrees with the archive majority (stationary, return-A late, B2 late on original-majority spans) it is armed by construction at every checkpoint, with no quantity in its arming that changes between checkpoint 2 and checkpoint 32 or between a switched and a stationary stream.

Design arithmetic from the simulator's known rates and published segment geometry (no score of this experiment exists): composed per-event disagreement rate 0.1625 (1/8 stochastic flip composed with 1/20 report flip), pure-segment agreement 0.8375, as in every preceding protocol in this line. Per-event opposed probability against a reference majority of the event's own rule: 0.1625 raw, about 0.13 after the matched-share adjustment (about 0.80 of events are matched non-neutral); against a majority of the opposite rule: 0.8375 raw, about 0.67 adjusted. Leg-S retention: P(at least 1 opposed among 6 same-rule events) = 1 - (1 - p)^6 = 0.655 at p = 0.1625 and 0.566 at p = 0.13; P(at least 1 opposed among 2 opposite-rule + 4 same-rule events) = 1 - (1 - 0.8375)^2 (1 - 0.1625)^4 = 0.987 raw and 1 - (1 - 0.67)^2 (1 - 0.13)^4 = 0.938 adjusted. Reference-window composition by checkpoint (newest window 2, reference window 50, segments 240 / 64 / 48): checkpoint 2 design purity 0.8375, checkpoint 4 0.8105, checkpoint 8 0.7565, checkpoint 16 0.6485, checkpoint 32 0.5675 global (realized higher under self-fit; graded purity experiment realized checkpoint-32 purity ranges 0.645-0.758 / 0.658-0.810 with the gate armed at 3/9 states per cohort, and realized onset purity armed at every pooled onset state on both cohorts).

Handoff section 8 standing limitations: weak uncertainty calibration and excessive abstention remain listed persistent weaknesses. An abstention branch that can fire a full 16-task refusal at a stationary checkpoint 32 - with no release condition ever evaluated - is the sharpest realized instance of excessive abstention in this line: the refusal is costless in harm and total in lost productivity, and it alone decided the preceding experiment's only failed criterion.

checkpoints.note: A checkpoint value k means the learner has observed the full A history plus the first k TRAIN events of the named stage (control: first k continuation events). Checkpoints 2 and 4 together are the pooled onset window for criteria 1, 2, 3, and 4; 32 grades release (criterion 5, with its new abstention sub-condition) and is part of the stationary population for criterion 6 (this experiment's PRIMARY criterion); 8 and 16 report persistence costs, including the abstention gate's leg trajectories (realized purity against the design values and realized acting-window opposed counts). Checkpoint values are benchmark bookkeeping only: the learner never receives k, a stage name, or any elapsed-since-switch count (see permitted_observations); the reference purity, the acting-window opposed count, and all windows are fixed observed-stream summaries, not segment measurements - the design values by checkpoint are consequences of the published segment geometry acting on those summaries, not inputs to the learner. Checkpoint 0 is a reported diagnostic, NOT graded: at k=0 the stream contains zero post-switch events, so no evidence-driven learner can distinguish the switched world from the pre-switch world.

simulator.family: StochasticWorld exactly as implemented in benchmarks/stochastic_prequential_benchmark.py (SameSchemaWorld two public numeric features inlet/outlet, anonymous actions, authored span-to-effect bands). No simulator code is changed by this experiment; the benchmark harness for this experiment reuses StochasticWorld and public_train unchanged.
simulator.hidden_rules: Hidden physics schedule per seed: A (original progress/damage mapping) -> B1 (progress/damage inverted) -> return_A (original) -> B2 (inverted). Phase boundaries, phase names, and the active rule are benchmark-private and are never supplied to any learner.
simulator.true_stochastic_feedback: Every actual non-neutral simulator action has probability 1/8 of a progress/damage flip, drawn by deterministic sha256 of (seed, split, episode index, action id, tick) exactly as in StochasticWorld._sample_outcome. Neutral outcomes stay neutral. TEST outcomes are the realized stochastic outcomes, not clean deterministic ones.
simulator.reported_feedback: An independent sha256 draw on (seed, TRAIN episode index) flips a non-neutral TRAIN reported progress/damage label with probability 1/20, exactly as in public_train. The learner receives only the possibly corrupted public report. Actual actor harm and label flips are counted separately by the benchmark.
simulator.actor: Independent hash-seeded random first-action actor, one action per disposable TRAIN episode, identical stream for every method. The learner issues ZERO training interventions of its own (acquisition budget = 0; see budgets).
simulator.stationary_control_arm: A separate arm per seed with NO rule change: 240 A TRAIN episodes (indices 1000..1239) followed by 64 further A TRAIN episodes (indices 5000..5063, physics original). It measures gate selectivity when nothing changed - false recovery, false minority engagement, false abstention, lost productivity - and is this experiment's PRIMARY population: the graded purity failure occurred here (one full abstention at control checkpoint 32), the reference window never mixes segments on this arm (design purity the pure-segment level 0.8375 at every control checkpoint, so leg P is designed armed throughout and leg S is the only leg that can release a stationary abstention), and the acting window is single-segment throughout.

permitted_observations: The learner sees only the public reported stream of {features, progress, damage} events in chronological order, identical for every method, plus the public TEST frame (actions with public features) at decision time. No phase label, rule identity, episode index, checkpoint value, stage position, true (unflipped) outcome, report-flip flag, simulator state, or TEST outcome may enter the learner, its signals, its concordance tests, its minority set or minority fraction, its authority condition, its reference purity, its acting-window opposition count, its recovery models, or its checkpoint record. In particular the abstention release gate is computed from reported events, their spans, the extended reference window's own per-span majorities, and the last 8 observed events only: the learner has no access to how many events have elapsed since any switch, to which events belonged to any segment, or to whether any segment exists - the purity fraction and the acting-window opposed count are fixed observed-stream summaries, not segment or switch detectors fed with privileged boundaries.

training_indices.control_A_continuation: 5000..5063 (64 episodes, physics original, stationary control arm only)

test.repeated_indices_note: The same TEST indices are re-scored at every checkpoint by every method; checkpoint rows are therefore not independent samples. TEST is read-only: no TEST outcome is ever trained on, and the harness must verify each method's checkpoint record is unchanged after TEST evaluation (contamination check, as in stochastic_prequential_benchmark).

candidate.name: AbstentionReleaseGatedRecoveryMemory
candidate.placement: New separate optional learner class in developmental_ai/. The default controller and every existing learner are untouched; existing learners appear only as baselines. The graded EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory, EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory, BoundedAuthorityJointRecoveryMemory, LongDisagreementJointRecoveryMemory, ExtendedReferenceJointRecoveryMemory, MinorityArchiveJointRecoveryMemory, and ReferencePurityGatedRecoveryMemory are baselines in this experiment, not modified by it.

fixed_parameters.acting_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory (existing estimator: engineered max-minus-min span statistic, 0.25 Laplace smoothing as coded in relation_outcome_memory.py) fitted on the LAST 8 observed public events only - identically the recent8 baseline, exactly as in the graded guard, retained-recovery, joint, bounded, long-disagreement, extended-reference, minority-archive, and reference-purity candidates.
fixed_parameters.immediate_signal: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference, minority-archive, and reference-purity candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned: for each of the newest 2 events, a hard span-majority expectation over the 50 events immediately preceding the newest window (indices N-52 .. N-3); strictly-highest reported class wins, tie or empty gives null; an event is matched if expectation and reported class are both progress or damage, and opposed if matched and different; opposed_count in 0..2; no fitted probabilities anywhere. The decision record ALSO carries the legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only, never a decision input), exactly as in the graded candidates, so the graded long candidate's rule remains derivable from the records alone.
fixed_parameters.retained_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: every observed event BEFORE the original reference partition, indices 0 .. N-27, i.e. events[:N-26]. Not phase-segmented, not a snapshot, and receives no phase, stage, or switch information.
fixed_parameters.archive_concordance_test: IDENTICAL per-event definition to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, the archive expectation is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among ALL archive events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null); e is archive-MATCHED if its expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is archive-CONCORDANT if archive-matched and its reported class EQUALS the expectation. concordant_count and archive_matched_count are in 0..2 and are recorded in full. Raw integer counts only.
fixed_parameters.joint_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, e is JOINT if it is archive-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference) on the SAME event. joint_count in 0..2.
fixed_parameters.recovery_model: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the retained archive events only (events[:N-26]), with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose).
fixed_parameters.authority_condition: IDENTICAL to the graded long-disagreement, extended-reference, minority-archive, and reference-purity candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned - all three legs, computed from the observed reported stream only, using the same span-majority machinery: (A) LOCAL-ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT (local window = last 26 events; stable_disagreement iff comparable C >= 1 AND disagreeing D satisfies D * 2 > C); (B) ACTING-WINDOW ARCHIVE CONCORDANCE (recent_concordant_count = archive-concordant events among the last 8, in 0..8); (C) PRECEDING-WINDOW ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT (preceding window = 26 events immediately before the local window; preceding_stable_disagreement iff C2 >= 1 AND D2 * 2 > C2; long_disagreement iff stable_disagreement AND preceding_stable_disagreement). BRANCH AUTHORITY for the carried-over branches, unchanged: ABSTENTION armed (before the new release gate) iff NOT stable_disagreement; RECOVERY armed (before the carried-over purity gate) iff NOT stable_disagreement OR recent_concordant_count >= 2 OR long_disagreement. Would-have-fired disarmed branches are recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire / minority_would_fire) and fall through. The new release gate is an ADDITIONAL condition on the abstention branch only (see abstention_release_gate); it does not modify any leg of this condition, and this condition does not enter the gate's computations beyond the abstention arming it already supplied. No fitted probability, phase, stage, checkpoint, or elapsed-since-switch count enters either condition.
fixed_parameters.minority_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded minority-archive and reference-purity candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned. Computed from the retained archive (events[:N-26]) and its own per-span majorities only. For each archive event e: let M(e) be the archive expectation for span(e) under the unchanged archive concordance definition (strictly-highest reported class among archive events of that span; tie or empty gives null). e is ARCHIVE-MATCHED if M(e) is progress or damage AND e's reported class is progress or damage. e is MINORITY (discordant) if archive-matched AND e's reported class DIFFERS from M(e). The MINORITY SET is the set of all minority archive events, in chronological order. minority_matched_count (over the archive) = number of archive-matched archive events; minority_discordant_count = size of the minority set; minority_fraction = minority_discordant_count / minority_matched_count (0 if minority_matched_count == 0). All three counts and the fraction are recorded at every checkpoint.
fixed_parameters.minority_arming: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: the minority branch is ARMED (before the carried-over purity gate) iff minority_fraction >= 0.25 AND minority_discordant_count >= 8. When the branch is not armed it cannot be taken, whatever the minority joint count says; a would-have-fired disarmed minority branch is recorded (minority_would_fire) and falls through.
fixed_parameters.minority_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, the MINORITY EXPECTATION for span(e) is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among MINORITY-SET events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is MINORITY-MATCHED if its minority expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is MINORITY-CONCORDANT if minority-matched and its reported class EQUALS the minority expectation. minority_concordant_count and minority_matched_count (over the newest window) are in 0..2 and are recorded in full, with per-event minority records exactly as in the graded candidates.
fixed_parameters.minority_joint_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, e is MINORITY-JOINT if it is MINORITY-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference, unchanged) - both flags on the SAME event. minority_joint_count in 0..2, recorded in full with per-event minority joint flags.
fixed_parameters.minority_model: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the MINORITY SET events only, with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose).
fixed_parameters.reference_purity_gate: CARRIED OVER IDENTICALLY from the graded reference-purity candidate, unchanged and not re-tuned, and applied to the two RECOVERY branches exactly as graded there. Computed from the extended reference window (the 50 events immediately preceding the newest window, indices N-52 .. N-3 - the SAME window the immediate signal reads) and its own per-span majorities only. For each reference event e: let R(e) be the reference expectation for span(e), i.e. the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among REFERENCE events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is REFERENCE-MATCHED if R(e) is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is REFERENCE-CONCORDANT if reference-matched AND e's reported class EQUALS R(e). reference_matched_count and reference_concordant_count are over the 50 reference events; reference_purity = reference_concordant_count / reference_matched_count (0 if reference_matched_count == 0). The purity gate is ARMED iff reference_purity >= 0.70. Regular recovery fires iff joint_count >= 1 AND the carried-over recovery authority is armed AND the purity gate is armed; minority recovery fires iff minority_joint_count >= 1 AND the minority branch is armed AND the purity gate is armed (and regular recovery did not fire, per the decision order). A recovery trigger blocked by purity alone is recorded (recovery_disarmed_by_purity / minority_disarmed_by_purity) and falls through. In THIS experiment the same purity quantity and threshold additionally enter the abstention branch through the new release gate below - as one leg of that gate, with the quantity, its window, and its threshold all unchanged; the gate's second leg is the only other new element, and the two legs together are the single changed element of this experiment (one new gate, on one branch).
fixed_parameters.abstention_release_gate: THE SINGLE NEW ELEMENT OF THIS EXPERIMENT. A release gate on the ABSTENTION branch only; the recovery branches, their authority condition, the purity gate as applied to them, the minority branch, the acting model, and every carried-over definition are unchanged. The abstention branch fires iff ALL of the following hold: (i) the carried-over trigger and arming hold (opposed_count == 2 AND abstention authority armed, i.e. NOT stable_disagreement); (ii) LEG P - the reference-purity gate is armed (reference_purity >= 0.70, the identical quantity and threshold that bound the recovery branches); and (iii) LEG S - ACTING-WINDOW OPPOSITION SUPPORT: acting_opposed_count >= 3, where acting_opposed_count is the number of opposed events among the LAST 8 observed events, each of those 8 events scored against the SAME extended-reference per-span majorities used by the immediate signal (an acting-window event is matched / opposed under the identical hard span-majority definition: expectation = strictly-highest reported class among the 50 reference events of that span, tie or empty gives null; matched iff expectation and reported class are both progress or damage; opposed iff matched and different). The newest 2 events are the last 2 of the acting window, so acting_opposed_count includes the triggering pair: whenever the trigger holds (opposed_count == 2), leg S is equivalently the requirement that at least ONE of the 6 acting-window events preceding the newest window is also opposed (supporting_opposed_count = acting_opposed_count - opposed_count >= 1). An abstention trigger whose carried-over arming holds but which the release gate blocks is recorded and falls through to recent8: abstention_disarmed_by_purity is true iff leg P alone blocked it (purity disarmed, leg S satisfied), abstention_disarmed_by_support is true iff leg S alone blocked it (support count below threshold, purity armed), and both flags are true iff both legs blocked it; both flags are FALSE when the carried-over authority was already disarmed (the release gate did not block that state - the authority did, exactly as in the graded candidates) and when the branch is taken. All gate quantities are recorded at every checkpoint: the per-event acting-window opposition records for all 8 acting-window events (span, reference-set event count for that span, reference majority class or null, reported class, matched flag, opposed flag), acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, the support threshold, purity_armed (already recorded with the purity record), abstention_gate_armed (the conjunction of legs P and S), and the two disarmed flags. No fitted probability, phase, stage, checkpoint, or elapsed-since-switch count enters the computation: both legs are fixed observed-stream summaries of windows this candidate family already computes (the 50-event reference window and the 8-event acting window).
fixed_parameters.decision_rule: Evaluated in this exact order on every decision once the signals are evaluable: (1) RECOVERY - if joint_count >= 1 AND the recovery branch is armed (carried-over authority) AND the purity gate is armed, act through the recovery model (source recorded as retained_archive), exactly as the graded reference-purity candidate. (2) MINORITY RECOVERY - else if minority_joint_count >= 1 AND the minority branch is armed (minority_fraction >= 0.25 AND minority_discordant_count >= 8) AND the purity gate is armed, act through the minority model (source recorded as minority_archive), exactly as the graded reference-purity candidate. (3) ABSTENTION - else if opposed_count == 2 AND the abstention branch is armed (carried-over authority) AND the abstention release gate is armed (leg P purity armed AND leg S acting_opposed_count >= 3), abstain (choose returns None). (4) RECENT8 - otherwise act through the acting model exactly. A branch whose trigger fires while the branch is disarmed - by its own arming, by the carried-over authority, by the purity gate, or (abstention only) by the release gate's support leg - is recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire / minority_would_fire, plus recovery_disarmed_by_purity / minority_disarmed_by_purity where purity alone blocked a recovery branch, and abstention_disarmed_by_purity / abstention_disarmed_by_support where the release gate blocked abstention) and falls through. There is no other input: no stage, phase, rule, or switch information, and no fitted probability enters any branch.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule_rationale: Every preceding cycle in this line bounded a recovery branch; the abstention branch was left with its original bounded-authority arming because, in the graded minority evaluation, it happened to release perfectly (0/144 checkpoint-32 abstentions on both cohorts). The graded purity records show that release was luck, not structure: the branch's arming contains no quantity that varies between a stationary stream and a switched one, or between checkpoint 2 and checkpoint 32, so on the purity cohorts it fired a full stationary refusal that decided criterion 6 and supplied the last unreleased checkpoint-32 state under criterion 5. This cycle therefore gives abstention the same TREATMENT the recovery branches received - an evidence-derived release condition built from summaries the candidate already computes - rather than a new signal: leg P reuses the reference-purity quantity unchanged (its segment-composition separation is the family's one demonstrated onset-vs-late separator: armed at every pooled onset state on both graded purity cohorts, armed at only 3 of 9 checkpoint-32 states on each), and leg S adds the minimal corroboration step for a two-event trigger (the pair must not be the acting window's only opposition), in the same style as the recovery authority's corroboration leg (at least 2 archive-concordant events among the last 8) in the bounded-authority experiment. The design deliberately does NOT re-threshold any carried-over count (the purity threshold stays at 0.70, the abstention trigger stays at opposed_count == 2, the corroboration-style support threshold is the minimal step above the trigger itself, 3 of 8), and it deliberately does NOT claim the two legs identify WHY a pair is opposed: on stationary evidence a flipped pair is locally identical to an onset pair (pre-registered in the hypothesis), so the gate is a calibrated evidence bar with a quantified onset cost, graded on both sides - not a switch detector.
fixed_parameters.action_scoring: Whichever model the decision rule selects, the choice is that model's RelationOutcomeMemory.choose output. An abstention is scored as a failed task, never as a success, and is reported separately.
fixed_parameters.minimum_events_rule: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference, minority-archive, and reference-purity candidates: the extended signal (and with it the reference purity and the acting-window opposition count, which read the same 50-event reference window) requires a 2-event newest window and a full 50-event reference window (at least 52 observed events); the archive concordance test requires at least 27. Below 52 events the extended signal, the purity gate, and the abstention release gate are not evaluable, reference_purity is recorded as 0 with purity_armed false and the per-event purity records empty, the acting-window opposition records are empty with acting_opposed_count and supporting_opposed_count recorded as 0 and abstention_gate_armed false, joint_count and minority_joint_count are recorded as 0 (their opposed side is not evaluable), and the learner acts with a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on all available events (recorded as not evaluable, gate_evaluable false). Every benchmark checkpoint in this experiment has at least 240 observed events, so all windows are full and the fallback is never exercised during evaluation; it exists only so the class is well-defined for unit tests on short synthetic streams.
fixed_parameters.checkpoint: Append-only public events only; record/restore by canonical SHA256 replay exactly as the existing memory classes; restoring must reproduce the full decision record (extended-reference signal records, legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only), archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, the full authority record, the full minority record, the full purity record, AND the full abstention-gate record - per-event acting-window opposition records over the last 8 events, acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, abstention_gate_armed flag, abstention_disarmed_by_purity and abstention_disarmed_by_support flags - all counts, branch taken, acting source) and the choice identically. Maximum 1000 recorded events (existing MAX_SAMPLES).
fixed_parameters.threshold_justification: Fixed a priori from the simulator's known noise rates, the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates and decision records, and this simulator's published segment geometry, not from any score of this experiment (none exist). (i) PURITY THRESHOLD 0.70: carried over UNCHANGED from the graded reference-purity protocol - the identical quantity (reference-concordant fraction over the extended reference window's matched non-neutral events), the identical window (50 events), the identical threshold. It is not re-derived and not re-tuned here; its design values by checkpoint (0.8375 / 0.8105 / 0.7565 / 0.6485 / 0.5675 global for checkpoints 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32) and its realized behavior on the graded purity cohorts (armed at every pooled onset state on both cohorts; armed at 3 of 9 checkpoint-32 states on each) are the published evidence this cycle builds on. Applying an already-frozen quantity to one more branch is not a new fitted parameter. (ii) SUPPORT THRESHOLD acting_opposed_count >= 3: the minimal corroboration step above the carried-over trigger - the trigger itself contributes exactly 2 opposed events (the newest window), so the threshold requires exactly ONE further opposed event among the 6 preceding acting-window events, no more. Any higher threshold (4+) would require two corroborating events and, by the rates below, would cut checkpoint-2 onset retention to about 0.18, deleting most of the branch's graded onset protection; any lower value is the trigger itself (no gate). Retention arithmetic from the composed rates (per-event opposed probability about 0.1625 raw / 0.13 matched-adjusted against an own-rule majority; about 0.8375 raw / 0.67 adjusted against an opposite-rule majority): stationary and checkpoint-2 onset states (6 preceding acting-window events all of the reference's own rule) retain with probability 1 - (1 - p)^6 = 0.566-0.655; checkpoint-4 onset states (2 opposite-rule + 4 own-rule among the 6) retain with probability 0.938-0.987; pooled onset retention (checkpoints 2 and 4 equally weighted) about 0.75-0.82 for leg S alone and about 0.72-0.78 combined with leg P at its onset design arming (about 0.95; realized 1.00 across pooled onset states on both graded purity cohorts). Late checkpoint-32 survival: leg P armed share realized 3/9 per cohort in the graded purity experiment times leg-S retention about 0.57-0.66 (the 6 preceding acting-window events at checkpoint 32 follow the current rule, whose majority dominates the mixed reference) gives about 0.19-0.22 per triggered late state. (iii) All other carried-over thresholds are UNCHANGED and not re-tuned: newest window 2, extended reference 50, legacy reference 24, archive events[:N-26], local window 26, preceding window 26, recovery threshold joint_count >= 1, abstention trigger opposed_count == 2, strict-majority rule D * 2 > C in both authority windows, corroboration recent_concordant_count >= 2, minority fraction threshold 0.25, minority count floor 8, minority joint threshold 1, purity threshold 0.70. The only new fixed parameter is the support threshold 3 (of 8), derived above from the published noise rates alone.

expected_failure_modes: Stationary false pair surviving both legs (pre-registered, the cycle's central risk): leg P is designed ARMED on stationary evidence (design purity 0.8375; the graded failure state realized 0.886) and does not release stationary abstention at all; leg S releases a stationary trigger only when none of the 6 preceding acting-window events is opposed (probability about 0.34-0.43 per triggered state). A stationary opposed pair WITH one supporting opposed event among the preceding 6 therefore still fires a full 16-task abstention, and a single such state at a control checkpoint where recent8 scores about 10 or more is by itself likely to fail criterion 6's successes sub-condition (margin 6) unless offset by productive control recovery elsewhere, exactly as the development cohort of the graded purity experiment was offset (+6 from one control recovery) and the additional cohort was not. This outcome is charged against criterion 6, not excused, and the report must state the surviving state's realized purity, acting_opposed_count, and supporting count.

Onset abstention thinning costing the harm guards (pre-registered): the gate retains only about 0.72-0.78 of the reference-purity candidate's pooled onset abstentions by design - the lost firings are concentrated at checkpoint 2 (retention about 0.57-0.66 there) and at B1 onset, where abstention is the family's only protective response (recovery is archive-discordant-blocked and the minority branch is unarmed there by design). Each lost firing returns 16 tasks to recent8 play at onset harm rates of roughly 8-14 per state; against the graded purity margins (criterion 3: 58 / 85 pooled harm below the guard; criterion 1(c) B2: 16 / 29 below the guard; criterion 4: 42 / 25 below the guard) a typical draw is designed to pass, but an unlucky cohort - several lost B1 firings, or lost firings concentrated in one cell - can fail criterion 3's per-cell sub-condition (at least 5 of 6 cells at or below recent8 becomes easier, not harder, when abstention is lost, since recent8 play equals recent8 harm; the binding risk is the guard comparison in criterion 3(a) and criteria 1(c) / 4) and is charged, not excused. Realized gate disarmings are recorded at every onset state (split by leg), so a thinning failure is fully distinguishable from a trigger failure in the report.

Late abstention surviving the gate at checkpoint 32 (pre-registered): leg P's realized checkpoint-32 arming on the graded purity cohorts was 3 of 9 states per cohort (self-fit compression raised realized purity to 0.645-0.810 against the 0.5675 global design value), so a late state with purity at or above 0.70 AND a supporting opposed event (combined survival about 0.19-0.22 per triggered state) still takes the abstained branch and fails criterion 5's new sub-condition (d) (0 of 9 abstained states) even while sub-conditions (a)-(c) pass. That outcome would show the release gate's late leg is too weak on realized (self-fitted) purity values, and would redirect the next cycle toward an expiry summary that is not self-fitted, under its own new protocol - the same redirect the purity protocol pre-registered for its own failure mode 2.

Purity leg disarming onset abstention on purity noise (pre-registered, smaller than in the purity experiment because abstention is a thinner branch): the checkpoint-4 design purity is 0.8105, about 1.6 sd above the 0.70 threshold at roughly 40 matched reference events, so on an unlucky cohort an onset state can realize purity below 0.70 and lose an abstention firing the reference-purity candidate would have taken (its recovery branches faced the same risk in the graded experiment and realized zero onset disarmings on both cohorts; abstention states are fewer, so the expected count is lower, but any realized onset purity disarming is recorded and charged against criteria 1, 3, and 4 through the lost protection).

Support-count span sparsity: the acting-window opposition records score 8 events against reference majorities fitted on about 5-6 events per span; on spans absent from the reference the expectation is null and the event is unmatched (not opposed), so acting_opposed_count can read low on thin-span draws at ANY checkpoint, including genuine onset states - a further, unmodeled thinning of onset abstention beyond the rate arithmetic in threshold_justification, visible in the recorded per-event acting-window records and charged like failure mode 2 if it binds.

Interaction with the recovery branches at B2 and return-A (bounded, recorded): the release gate sits BELOW both recovery branches in the decision order, so it cannot displace a recovery firing; but at states where the graded candidates abstained because recovery was purity-disarmed (the graded purity experiment's additional return-A checkpoint-32 state is one: a purity-disarmed recovery fell through to abstention), this candidate falls through one step further to recent8 when the gate also blocks the abstention - at that graded state recent8 scored 2/14 against the abstention's 0/0 and the ungated recovery's 13/3, so the fall-through can ADD harm at individual late states while removing the abstention from the records. Criterion 5's harm is not directly graded (its successes sub-condition is), but checkpoint-32 successes and harm are reported in full and any such state is named in the report.

Minority-model flip-symmetry limit (carried over, stated): the minority branch this candidate carries exploits this simulator's exact-inversion structure (original-segment flip reports reinforce the inverted class in the minority pool). The abstention release gate itself is structure-agnostic (it reads only opposition counts against reference majorities and reference self-agreement), but any PASS remains bounded to this inversion simulator: release of an ungated abstention branch by reference purity plus acting-window opposition corroboration, not a general excessive-abstention solution, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.

baselines.name: recent8
baselines.role: Simplest credible baseline and the candidate's own acting model: relation model on the last 8 observed events only.
baselines.in: all criteria comparisons as named; every candidate-vs-recent8 difference is attributable to the decision rule (now including its minority branch, purity gate, and abstention release gate) alone

baselines.name: reference_purity_gated_recovery
baselines.role: ReferencePurityGatedRecoveryMemory, the preceding experiment's candidate (graded Partially demonstrated): identical acting model, identical extended signal, identical archive and concordance definitions, identical joint test, identical recovery model, identical abstention trigger and carried-over abstention arming, identical three-leg authority condition, identical minority branch, and the identical reference-purity gate on its recovery branches, differing ONLY in that its abstention branch carries NO release gate (no purity leg, no support leg). This is the decisive comparison for this experiment: candidate-vs-reference-purity-candidate differences isolate the abstention release gate alone, on the stationary control arm above all (criterion 6), at checkpoint 32 (criterion 5), and at onset (criteria 1, 3, 4).
baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criteria 1-6 comparisons in the report (its totals are the decisive gate comparison, not PASS/FAIL comparators beyond the criteria as named)

baselines.name: minority_archive_joint_recovery
baselines.role: MinorityArchiveJointRecoveryMemory (graded Failed / Regression at checkpoint 32): the reference-purity candidate minus the purity gate - the ungated-abstention reference point whose control abstentions were 0/240 on both of its cohorts and whose checkpoint-32 failures motivated the purity gate.
baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; checkpoint-32 and control comparisons in the report

baselines.name: extended_reference_joint_recovery
baselines.role: ExtendedReferenceJointRecoveryMemory (graded Partially demonstrated): the minority candidate minus the minority branch - the checkpoint-32 reference point for the regular branch alone (its worse-cohort checkpoint-32 deficit pattern sets this protocol's Regression line, as in the preceding protocols).
baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; checkpoint-32 and B2 comparisons in the report

baselines.name: evidence_opposition_guard
baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory (graded Demonstrated): the 24-event-reference signal and acting model, with abstention as its only protective response - and, critically for this experiment, an UNGATED abstention branch whose graded control record was 0/15 abstention states on both of its cohorts (the base rate this cycle's stationary lottery is drawn from). Criteria 1, 3, and 4 hold the candidate to the guard's harm levels on the same cohort, exactly as in the preceding protocols.
baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criteria 1, 3, and 4 comparisons

baselines.name: long_disagreement_joint_recovery
baselines.role: LongDisagreementJointRecoveryMemory (graded Failed): the 24-event-reference predecessor with the full authority condition; its development criterion-5 failure by 1 success was a single late abstention state, part of this cycle's limitation evidence.

baselines.name: bounded_authority_joint_recovery
baselines.role: BoundedAuthorityJointRecoveryMemory (graded Failed): the two-leg authority predecessor in which the abstention arming this candidate carries (armed iff NOT stable_disagreement) was introduced.

baselines.name: joint_concordance_recovery
baselines.role: JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory (graded Failed): the unexpired joint candidate; its additional-cohort criterion-5 failure included a B1 checkpoint-32 abstention costing 9 successes, part of this cycle's limitation evidence.

baselines.name: cumulative
baselines.role: Relation model on all observed events. Plain cumulative retention remains the strongest simple retained comparator at return-A (it beat the reference-purity candidate on both axes on both cohorts) and is reported in full there; at B2 it is original-dominated and cannot protect the second switch.

baselines.name: evidence_opposition_retained_recovery
baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, the pooled both-events candidate (graded Failed): the engagement-sparsity reference point.

baselines.role: Relation model fitted on the first 192 events, never updated. The recovery target reference at return_A: what pure retained pre-switch knowledge scores there.

baselines.name: privileged_expected_oracle

acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_control_selectivity_restored_PRIMARY
acceptance_criteria.rule: PRIMARY criterion for this experiment - the graded reference-purity candidate FAILed it on the additional cohort (successes 110 vs recent8 120, required at least 114; the entire deficit one stationary abstention state at control checkpoint 32, seed 383017) and it is this cycle's selected limitation's first prong. Graded per cohort, on the stationary control arm pooled across checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 (240 episode-checkpoints), in the identical form carried through the preceding protocols: (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 32 of 240, AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 6, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions. The realized reference_purity, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, and abstention-gate flags on the control arm are recorded and reported at every checkpoint (design: purity at the pure-segment level 0.8375, leg P armed throughout; leg S is the only leg that can release a stationary abstention), alongside the realized minority_fraction and minority_armed values exactly as in the preceding protocols; the downstream totals are what is graded here, and every control checkpoint at which the release gate changed the taken branch relative to the records-only reference-purity-rule derivation (see metrics_reported) - in particular every abstention the gate blocked and every abstention that survived both legs - is stated explicitly in the report, with the surviving state's purity and support counts named. The graded reference-purity candidate PASSed this criterion on development (0/240 abstentions, 124 vs recent8 118 successes, 116 vs 122 harm, helped by one productive control recovery the gate does not touch); this cycle must hold development AND repair additional's failure mode on NEW cohorts, not merely re-draw it.

acceptance_criteria.name: release_and_productivity_by_checkpoint_32
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard - the graded reference-purity candidate PASSed it on both cohorts, with its one remaining additional non-recent8 state being the ungated abstention this cycle gates; carried sub-conditions (a)-(c) are unchanged in form and this cycle adds sub-condition (d), its headline tightening. Graded per cohort, pooled across stages B1, return_A, and B2 at checkpoint 32 (144 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 36 of 144 (25 percent), AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 8 (carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (c) from the candidate's decision records alone, among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 seed-checkpoint states (3 stages x 3 seeds), the candidate takes a non-recent8 branch (retained_archive, minority_archive, or abstained) in at most 1 state - the carried records-level release measure for the recovery branches - AND (d) NEW: the candidate takes the ABSTAINED branch in 0 of those 9 states (in the graded purity experiment the additional cohort's single counted state under (c) WAS an abstention; this cycle's hypothesis is that the release gate removes abstention from the late records entirely, so it is graded at zero, not at the carried allowance). The realized reference_purity, purity_armed, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, and both abstention-disarmed flags at all 9 states are reported alongside, split by branch taken, so the report distinguishes a gate release of abstention (trigger present, gate blocked it, fell through to recent8 - and by which leg) from a state where no abstention trigger was present at all, and likewise distinguishes the recovery branches' purity releases as in the preceding protocol.

acceptance_criteria.name: second_switch_B2_protection_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried over unchanged in form from the minority and reference-purity protocols: the abstention release gate must not give back the B2 protection the minority branch demonstrated (abstention is not the B2 protective branch - minority recovery is, and it sits above abstention in the decision order - but lost abstention firings at B2 states where neither recovery branch fired return those states to recent8 harm, and that is charged here). Graded per cohort over the B2 pooled onset cells (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds; 96 episode-checkpoints; engagement graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY, no TEST outcomes): (a) ENGAGEMENT - the minority recovery branch is TAKEN (minority_joint_count >= 1, minority branch armed, purity gate armed, acting source minority_archive) in at least 3 of the 6 pooled B2 onset seed-checkpoint states; AND (b) SELECTIVITY - the minority recovery branch is taken in at most 1 of the 6 pooled B1 onset states AND at most 1 of the 6 pooled return-A onset states on the same cohort; AND (c) HARM - candidate harmful TEST actions pooled over the B2 onset cells <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same cells on the same cohort, AND candidate B2 pooled onset harm <= 0.60 * recent8 B2 pooled onset harm on the same cohort; AND (d) PRODUCTIVITY - candidate successes pooled over the B2 onset cells >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16. Taken states are reported split by checkpoint (2 alone vs 4 alone vs pooled), with the realized minority_fraction, minority_armed flag, reference_purity, and purity_armed flag at each, and against the records-only minority-rule and reference-purity-rule derivations (see metrics_reported). Abstention-branch firing and abstention-gate disarmings at B2 are reported (with realized acting_opposed_count at each) but do NOT count toward sub-condition (a), as in the preceding protocols.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_onset_harm_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols: per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions over the same cells, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 0.60 * recent8 harmful TEST actions over the same cells. The graded reference-purity candidate PASSed it on both cohorts (37 vs guard 79 and ceiling 55.8; 29 vs guard 54 and ceiling 46.8, identical to the minority baseline on both) and this cycle must not give it back: at return-A onset the abstention branch is mostly disarmed by stable disagreement already, so the release gate's exposure here is small by construction, and any change is charged.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_recovery_successes_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate successes >= 40 percent of frozen_A successes pooled over the same cells (computed as candidate_successes * 5 >= frozen_A_successes * 2, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (b) candidate successes >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16 (carried over unchanged). Cumulative's, the joint candidate's, the bounded candidate's, the long candidate's, the extended candidate's, the minority candidate's, and the reference-purity candidate's return-A successes on the same cohort are reported alongside in full, and any shortfall is stated in the report, not hidden. The release gate sits below both recovery branches and does not enter this criterion's mechanism; it is carried so that any unexpected interaction (for example a fall-through change at a return-A onset state) is graded, not assumed away.

acceptance_criteria.name: pooled_onset_harm_not_above_guard
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across the six onset cells (stages B1, return_A, B2 x checkpoints 2 and 4; 288 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same six cells on the same cohort, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions in at least 5 of the 6 individual cells. Carried over unchanged from the graded joint, bounded, long, extended, minority, and reference-purity protocols. The graded reference-purity candidate PASSed it on both cohorts with margins of 58 and 85 harm below the guard (137 vs 195, 6/6 cells; 133 vs 218, 6/6) - those margins are this gate's onset budget: the hypothesis arithmetic prices the gate's onset abstention thinning at roughly 5-11 pooled harm, and this criterion grades whether the realized thinning stays inside the margin on NEW cohorts. Checkpoint 0 is reported but NOT graded.

acceptance_criteria.name: full_accounting
acceptance_criteria.rule: The saved detailed results contain every field listed in metrics_reported: per-seed TRAIN actor actual harm / productive / neutral, reported harm, label flips, learner acquisition actions (= 0), per-seed successes / harmful TEST actions / abstentions / attempted tasks for every method at every checkpoint, the candidate's full decision record (extended-reference signal records, legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only), archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, the full authority record, the full minority record, the full purity record, AND the full abstention-gate record: per-event acting-window opposition records over the last 8 events, acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, support threshold, abstention_gate_armed flag, abstention_disarmed_by_purity and abstention_disarmed_by_support flags - plus branch taken, recovery-fired flag, minority-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, acting source) at every checkpoint, checkpoint SHA256, and restore-replay identity. Any missing field fails this criterion regardless of scores.

budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 7). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.
budgets.harm_budget: Criterion 1(c): candidate B2 pooled onset harm at most the evidence_opposition_guard baseline's B2 pooled onset harm on the SAME cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's B2 pooled onset harm. Criterion 3: candidate pooled onset (all stages, checkpoints 2 and 4) harmful TEST actions at most the guard's pooled onset harm on the same cohort, with at least 5 of 6 individual onset cells at or below recent8. Criterion 4: candidate pooled return-A onset harm at most the guard's return-A onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's return-A onset harm. The onset abstention-thinning risk (expected failure mode 2) is charged against criteria 1, 3, and 4, not excused from them.
budgets.abstention_budget: Criteria 5 and 6 bound abstention's downstream cost at checkpoint 32 (at most 36 of 144, plus 0 abstained states among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states under criterion 5(d)) and on the stationary control arm (at most 32 of 240), as in the preceding protocols with this cycle's tightening. Abstention disarmed under stable disagreement is the carried-over release mechanism, not a budget violation; abstention blocked by the new release gate is recorded separately (abstention_disarmed_by_purity / abstention_disarmed_by_support) and is likewise not a budget violation - it is this experiment's mechanism, and its onset cost is graded through criteria 1, 3, and 4.

metrics_reported: Per seed, per stage (B1, return_A, B2, control), per checkpoint, per method: successes, harmful TEST actions, failed-by-abstention count, attempted tasks.

grading.format: Handoff section 6 report format. Every acceptance criterion above is graded PASS or FAIL individually, per cohort; no failed criterion may be hidden inside an overall positive summary. Criterion 6 is reported first among the criteria in the grading report, as this experiment's primary criterion; criteria 5, 1, and 4 (checkpoint-32 release with its abstention sub-condition, B2 protection, and return-A harm) are reported next, as its co-graded guards.
grading.demonstrated: All seven criteria PASS on BOTH cohorts, the historical transfer benchmark (benchmarks.transfer_benchmark, unchanged) still passes, and the full unit suite (python -m unittest discover -s tests) passes on the evaluation commit.
grading.failed: Criterion 6 FAILs on the additional cohort, or criterion 5 FAILs on the additional cohort, or any of criteria 1, 2, 3, or 4 FAILs on the additional cohort, or criterion 7 FAILs on either cohort.
grading.partially_demonstrated: Criterion 6 and criterion 7 PASS on both cohorts but criterion 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 FAILs on either cohort, or all criteria PASS on the development cohort only.
grading.regression: The candidate's pooled onset harm exceeds recent8's on both cohorts, or the candidate's stationary-control successes fall below recent8's by more than 6 on both cohorts, or the candidate's checkpoint-32 successes fall below recent8 - 4 on either cohort (the deficit line the graded minority candidate crossed on the additional cohort - 68 vs 82 - and, in the extended protocol's form, the graded extended candidate's worse-cohort deficit line), or the historical transfer benchmark or full unit suite breaks.
grading.generalization_level: At most handoff level 2-3 (choosing among / applying already-supplied representations under a rule change, plus designer-supplied signal, concordance, minority, routing, expiry, disagreement-age, reference-width, reference-purity, and abstention-release rules). No level-6 or novel-representation claim is permitted from this experiment: the A/B rules, span statistic, windows, archive definition, joint tests, minority definition and arming threshold, disagreement / corroboration / long-disagreement conditions, the reference-purity definition and threshold, the acting-window opposition definition and support threshold, and the decision rule are all designer-supplied, and the minority read the candidate carries exploits this simulator's exact-inversion structure (see expected failure mode 7). A PASS would demonstrate release of an ungated abstention branch - a stationary arm and checkpoint-32 record free of full-refusal states while the onset profile is preserved - in this simulator only, not general excessive-abstention handling, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.
grading.ci_claims: Linux/Windows validation is claimed only for an exact commit with a real GitHub Actions run on that commit; otherwise it is recorded as UNVERIFIED.

boundaries: No privileged simulator information to the learner; the oracle is a labeled reference only.
No learner-issued training interventions; all TRAIN evidence comes from the shared external actor stream.
No default controller promotion, no PR merge, no D1-D10 or V2A/V2B roadmap change, no AthenZ/Synveil integration (hard gates requiring the owner's explicit authorization).
Same engineered two-feature simulator family as the preceding switch experiments; results are not evidence of independent generalization, novel rule discovery, or real-world safety.
Preserve all negative results with the same prominence as positive ones.

Denominators in this protocol are exact: 16 TEST episodes per seed per checkpoint, 3 seeds per cohort, hence 48 episodes per stage-checkpoint cell, 96 per pooled return-A or B2 onset figure, and 288 per pooled all-stage onset figure. Decision-record denominators are seed-checkpoint states: 3 per stage per cohort at checkpoint 2 alone, 6 per stage per cohort pooled at checkpoints 2 and 4, 9 switch-stage states per cohort at checkpoint 32, and 15 graded control states per cohort (checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 x 3 seeds).
registration: This protocol is committed BEFORE any candidate implementation, unit test, benchmark harness, or score inspection for this experiment. Once either cohort is evaluated, its seeds are INSPECTED: no parameter, threshold, seed, checkpoint, or acceptance criterion in this file may be revised against those results. A revised hypothesis requires a NEW protocol file and NEW seed cohorts. No parameter of the eleven graded onset experiments (early_post_switch_adaptation, first_contact_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_retained_recovery, joint_concordance_recovery, bounded_authority_joint_recovery, long_disagreement_joint_recovery, extended_reference_joint_recovery, minority_archive_joint_recovery, reference_purity_gated_recovery, and the abstention guard counted once) was re-tuned against its inspected cohorts in designing this protocol: the acting model, the extended and legacy references, the retained archive, the archive concordance definition, the joint recovery test's form, the recovery model, the abstention trigger's form and threshold, the local-archive disagreement definition, the corroboration condition, the long-disagreement leg, the minority set definition, the minority concordance and joint tests, the minority arming condition (minority_fraction >= 0.25 with a count floor of 8), and the reference-purity definition and threshold (0.70) are reused EXACTLY as frozen in the reference-purity protocol (newest window 2, reference 50 / legacy 24, archive events[:N-26], local window last 26, preceding window 26 before it, recovery threshold joint_count >= 1, abstention threshold opposed_count == 2, stable_disagreement iff C >= 1 AND D * 2 > C in both windows, corroboration recent_concordant_count >= 2, purity threshold 0.70). The single new element - the abstention release gate (leg P: the already-frozen reference-purity arming applied to the abstention branch; leg S: acting_opposed_count >= 3 over the last 8 events against the same extended-reference majorities, i.e. at least one supporting opposed event beyond the triggering pair) - is informed only by the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates and decision records (their limitation evidence, including the per-state stationary and checkpoint-32 record decompositions in limitation_evidence), the simulator's known noise rates, and this simulator's published segment geometry (240 / 64 / 48 events), never by any score of this experiment (none exist) and never by any acting-window opposition count computed on any cohort (the quantity appears in no preceding experiment's records in this form).
